source_uncertainties: ASR: 'module 7 ... module two' (L31 0:22-0:45); the slide footer reads Module 07 Part B. 'e to the i kappa dot x ... e to the minus kappa prime dot x' (L31 1418 s) drops the i; the slide (f0040) has exp(-i kappa'.x). 'volume average over the cube 0 to n' (L31 1361 s) is 0 <= x_i <= script L (f0040). 'R cubed' (L32 183 s) is the cube of side script L. 'g bar' for the derivative in T2 is the lecturer's notation.

Spoken justification of the derivative rule (L32 10:50): 'ddx_j of g_hat is zero because g_hat is in Fourier space'. The slide (L32 f0020) writes the correct integration by parts; the chapter gives periodicity as the reason.
The slide calls (12.7) a 'balance equation for the kinetic energy at wavenumber kappa' (L31 f0022); it is a definition. The half of the kinetic energy is omitted on the slide and mentioned in speech.

The slide calls p/rho the 'dynamic pressure' (L33 f0036); the chapter writes kinematic pressure. The slide writes the transform of -Laplacian p in the Poisson equation (L33 f0053) with p although p_hat is the coefficient of p/rho.
The lecture calls e_1, e_2, e_3 direction cosines (L31 f0040); they are the unit vectors along the axes.
Spoken 'sum over all wavenumber magnitudes' (L31 4:50 and 8:20); the slide sums over the wavenumber vectors kappa = kappa_0 n.

Zero truncation errors / 'exact' / 'perfect solution' (L31 14:50, L32 15:10, slide L31 f0022): true of the derivative of a represented field, not of the computed solution (chapter section 'What the representation establishes and what it does not').
Division by kappa^2 in P_jk and p_hat without excluding kappa = 0 (L32, L33 slides).

The recordings stop at the pressure term (L33 27:20: 'in the next class we will put this all into the Navier-Stokes equations'); equation (12.19) is the chapter's one-line completion. Checked against Lecture 34 (-nljYKsaUwo): it opens (0:05 to about 4:10) by restating the pressure result of Lecture 33 and substituting it into the Navier-Stokes equation, which gives (12.19). (12.19) stays in this chapter and chapter 13 cites it.
T2 slide equation numbers (6.122)-(6.125) belong to the source book and are not used. T2-P9 is skipped in the recording (12:27).
Jet-case box size 1 m and L11 ~ l0 are assumptions of the chapter, not lecture values.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: None directly; the slides state periodicity and a cube of side script L large compared with L11.
sections.research_extension: Truncation kmax = sqrt(2)N/3 and Delta x/eta = 2.96/(kmax eta) (Yeung, Sreenivasan, Pope 2018, p. 064603-3).
sections.teaching_construction: Periodic-box model; jet case (nu 1.4607e-5 as in chapters 6, 8 and 10, l0 0.1 m, u0 2 m/s, Re0 1.37e4, eps = u0^3/l0 = 80, eta 7.90e-5 m, box 1 m, N = 6.4e3, 2.6e11 points); Taylor-Green vortex; random band-limited field.

sections.section: Why the equations are rewritten for each wavenumber
sections.lecture_material: Karman-Howarth equation for f(r,t) does not show the energy cascade; energy per wavenumber needs a spectral analysis; DNS of homogeneous turbulence in wavenumber space.
sections.research_extension: Yeung, Sreenivasan, Pope 2018, pp. 064603-2, -3: Fourier pseudospectral DNS in a periodic cube; errors that remain.

sections.section: A periodic velocity field is a sum of Fourier modes
sections.lecture_material: Series u = sum exp(i kappa.x) u_hat; periodic condition; cube and lowest wavenumber kappa0 = 2 pi/L; mode as cos + i sin; modes non-random.
sections.teaching_construction: Cost of periodicity: no scales above L, R_ij periodic so R(L e1) = R(0); sum over vectors not magnitudes; e_j are axis vectors, not direction cosines.

sections.section: Orthonormality of the modes and the coefficients of the series
sections.lecture_material: Wavenumber vector, Kronecker delta, box average, orthonormality (stated without proof), coefficient by orthonormality, conjugate symmetry; operator F_kappa (L32 5:30).
sections.teaching_construction: One-line orthonormality argument; zero mode is the box average; Taylor-Green coefficients.

sections.section: The energy of a mode and the energy of the box
sections.lecture_material: Slide expression E_hat = <u_hat* . u_hat>, called a balance equation; half omitted; DNS in wavenumber space.
sections.teaching_construction: Parseval's relation for the box, k = (1/2) sum E_hat under homogeneity, binned relation to E(kappa); correction of the slide wording (definition, not balance).

sections.lecture_material: Transform of a derivative is i kappa_j g_hat, derived on the slide by the product rule; operator on a derivative.
sections.teaching_construction: Correct reason (periodicity of h = g exp(-i kappa.x)); gradient, divergence, curl, Laplacian rules; central-difference factor sin(kh)/(kh) and its errors 36.3, 9.97, 2.55 %.

sections.section: The coefficients of the velocity: random, zero mean and perpendicular to the wavevector
sections.lecture_material: u_hat_j = F{u_j}; modes non-random, coefficients random; mean zero; conjugate symmetry; continuity gives kappa.u_hat = 0.
sections.teaching_construction: Expectation versus box average and the zeroth mode; two degrees of freedom; Taylor-Green check.

sections.lecture_material: Decomposition G = G_par + G_perp, e = kappa/kappa, P_jk = delta_jk - kappa_j kappa_k/kappa^2 (continued in L33 1:37-8:02).
sections.teaching_construction: Properties P kappa = 0, symmetry, idempotence, trace 2; Figure 12.1; parallel share 1/3 for iid components.

sections.section: The Navier-Stokes equations for the coefficients
sections.lecture_material: Transform of each term; time derivative becomes total derivative; viscous term -nu kappa^2 u_hat; pressure term -i kappa_j p_hat; nonlinear term G_hat_j; ODE (12.16).
sections.research_extension: Viscous term treated exactly by an integrating factor in pseudospectral DNS (Yeung, Sreenivasan, Pope 2018, p. 064603-3).
sections.teaching_construction: Coupled-system remark; decay rates 2 nu kappa^2 for the jet case; nu/eta^2 = 1/tau_eta; kappa = 0 equation.

sections.lecture_material: p_hat = F{p/rho}; kappa^2 p_hat = i kappa_j G_hat_j (Poisson equation); -i kappa_j p_hat = G_par; pressure balances -G_par.
sections.teaching_construction: Final equation (12.19) (the recordings stop before it); link to chapter 6 (6.12); kappa = 0; solenoidality preserved; Taylor-Green solved exactly.

sections.section: The nonlinear coefficient is a sum over pairs of modes
sections.teaching_construction: Convolution (12.20), triads, Taylor-Green triads; check against grid products (2.3e-15).

sections.lecture_material: Slide heading announces the balance equation for the kinetic energy of Fourier modes; not derived in the recordings.
sections.teaching_construction: Equation (12.21); pressure does no work on a mode; sum rule (12.22); link to D(kappa) of chapter 11.

sections.section: Executable check: modes, derivatives, projection, pressure and pairs
sections.teaching_construction: Program of 164 lines; identity checks on two flows; aliasing demonstration.

sections.section: What the representation establishes and what it does not
sections.lecture_material: Claim of zero truncation errors, exactness, perfect solution (L31 14:50 to 15:05, L32 15:10).
sections.research_extension: Yeung, Sreenivasan, Pope 2018, pp. 064603-2, -3, -11: truncation, aliasing, remaining errors.
sections.teaching_construction: Aliasing mechanism; periodic-box limits; closure problem in wavenumber space.

sections.lecture_material: Practice problems 7-10 of Tutorial 2 (orthonormality, Laplacian, zeroth mode, vorticity).
sections.teaching_construction: Six original exercises (compute, derive, check an assumption, counterexample, design).
